project.name: WZTrack Dev Environment
project.description: Infrastructure, containerisation, and tooling setup required to run WZTrack locally and prepare it for production deployment.

requirements.title: Containerised development environment via Docker Compose
requirements.description: All WZTrack services (API, frontend, database) must run as Docker containers orchestrated by a single docker-compose.yml. A developer must be able to start the full stack with one command.
requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- `docker compose up --build` starts all three services without manual intervention.
- No service depends on host-installed Python, Node, or PostgreSQL.
- Environment variables are loaded from a `.env` file at the project root.
- Containers restart unless explicitly stopped.

requirements.title: PostgreSQL database with persistent volume and health check
requirements.description: The database container must persist data across container restarts using a named Docker volume. The API container must not start until the database passes its health check.
requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- Named volume `wztrack_pgdata` survives `docker compose down` and retains data.
- `docker compose down -v` explicitly wipes the volume for a clean slate.
- API container declares `depends_on: db: condition: service_healthy`.
- Health check uses `pg_isready` with a 5 s interval and 10 retries.

requirements.title: API service configuration and secrets management via .env
requirements.description: All sensitive configuration (DB credentials, JWT keys, admin seed email) must be supplied through environment variables loaded from a `.env` file. No secrets may be committed to source control.
requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- `.env` is listed in `.gitignore`.
- An `.env.example` with placeholder values is committed.
- `pydantic-settings` loads all config via the `Settings` class in `config.py`.
- RS256 PEM keys are stored as single-line strings with `\n` as the line separator.

requirements.title: RS256 JWT key generation and correct PEM encoding in .env
requirements.description: The API uses RS256 asymmetric JWT signing. Private and public keys must be generated once, stored in `.env` with newlines encoded as `\n`, and correctly decoded at runtime by the FastAPI config layer.
requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- Keys generated with `openssl genrsa` and `openssl rsa -pubout`.
- `.env` stores each PEM key as a single-line string with literal `\n` between lines.
- `config.py` `jwt_private_key_pem` property replaces `\\n` with `\n` before use.
- Login endpoint returns `token_type: bearer` with no JWT decode errors.

requirements.title: Python dependency pinning for runtime compatibility
requirements.description: The API Docker image must pin all Python dependencies to exact versions that are known to work together. Transitive incompatibilities must be resolved before they reach the image build.
requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- `requirements.txt` pins `bcrypt==3.2.2` to prevent passlib incompatibility with bcrypt 4.x.
- `pydantic[email]` is used (not plain `pydantic`) so `EmailStr` fields validate correctly.
- `fastapi==0.111.1` is pinned to avoid route assertion regressions.
- `docker compose up --build` completes with exit code 0.

requirements.title: FastAPI route annotation compliance for 204 responses
requirements.description: FastAPI 0.111+ asserts that HTTP 204 routes do not declare a response body type. All route functions that return 204 must not carry a `-> None` return annotation.
requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- No route decorated with `status_code=204` has a `-> None` return type annotation.
- API container starts without `AssertionError` from FastAPI internals.
- Affected routers: auth, issues, projects, testcases, users, wiki.

requirements.title: Nginx reverse proxy with correct host header and port forwarding
requirements.description: The nginx container proxies `/api/` requests to the API container. When running on a non-standard port (e.g. 8080), nginx must forward the full `Host` header including the port so that FastAPI redirect responses produce correct `Location` URLs.
requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- `proxy_set_header Host $http_host` is used (not `$host`).
- Trailing-slash redirects from FastAPI resolve to the correct port (not port 80).
- No CORS `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` errors appear in the browser console.
- `GET http://localhost:8080/api/v1/projects/` returns HTTP 200.

requirements.title: Port allocation strategy for Windows with Rancher Desktop
requirements.description: On Windows with Rancher Desktop, port 80 is owned by the `host-switch` process and cannot be bound by Docker containers. The frontend must be exposed on a different port.
requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- Frontend nginx container is mapped to `8080:80` in docker-compose.yml.
- `CORS_ORIGINS` env var includes `http://localhost:8080`.
- No port conflict errors on `docker compose up`.
- Developer documentation notes that Docker Desktop and Rancher Desktop use different named pipes.

requirements.title: Admin seed user with valid email domain
requirements.description: The API seeds an admin user on first startup using credentials from environment variables. The admin email must use a domain accepted by `email-validator` (pydantic's EmailStr).
requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- Admin email uses a non-reserved TLD (`.io`, `.com`, `.dev` — not `.local`).
- Seeding is idempotent: running twice does not create duplicate users.
- Default admin credentials documented in `.env.example` and the wiki.

requirements.title: Database migration strategy before production deployment
requirements.description: The current `create_all` call on startup is acceptable for development but must be replaced with Alembic migrations before any production deployment to allow schema evolution without data loss.
requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- Alembic is initialised with `alembic init`.
- At least one baseline migration captures the current schema.
- `alembic upgrade head` runs cleanly against a fresh database.
- `docker compose up` runs migrations before starting the API.

requirements.title: Docker context configuration for Rancher Desktop on Windows
requirements.description: Rancher Desktop uses the `default` Docker context (npipe `docker_engine`), not the `desktop-linux` context created by Docker Desktop. The correct context must be active for all Docker and Compose commands to work.
requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- `docker context use default` documented in setup guide.
- `docker context ls` shows `default` as active.
- Any stale `desktop-linux` context has been removed.
- CI pipeline explicitly sets the Docker context before running Compose commands.

requirements.title: JWT token invalidation via blocklist on logout
requirements.description: The current logout endpoint is stateless and does not invalidate the token. A token blocklist must be implemented so that a logged-out token is rejected before its natural expiry.
requirements.acceptance_criteria:
- Redis (or DB-backed) blocklist stores revoked JTI values until token expiry.
- Logout adds the token JTI to the blocklist.
- Middleware rejects requests carrying a blocklisted token with HTTP 401.
- Blocklist entries expire automatically when the token would have expired.

wiki.title: Environment setup guide
wiki.content:
# Environment setup guide

## Before you begin

- Windows 10/11 with Rancher Desktop installed and running
- Docker context set to `default`: run `docker context use default`
- Git configured with your credentials
- Ports 8080 and 8000 available

## Steps

1. Clone the repository.
2. Copy `.env.example` to `.env`.
3. Generate RS256 keys (see **Key generation** below) and paste into `.env`.
4. Set `ADMIN_EMAIL` to a valid address (not `.local` TLD).
5. Run `docker compose up --build` from the `wztrack/` directory.
6. Access the app at `http://localhost:8080`.
7. Log in with the admin credentials from your `.env`.

## Key generation

```bash
openssl genrsa -out private.pem 2048
openssl rsa -in private.pem -pubout -out public.pem
```

Paste each file into `.env` as a single line, replacing every newline with `\n`:

```
JWT_PRIVATE_KEY=-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----\nMIIEo...\n-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
JWT_PUBLIC_KEY=-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\nMIIBIj...\n-----END PUBLIC KEY-----
```

## Port reference

| Service | Host port | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Frontend (nginx) | 8080 | Port 80 reserved by Rancher Desktop on Windows |
| API (uvicorn) | 8000 | Direct access for testing |
| PostgreSQL | not exposed | Internal only |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Cannot connect to Docker daemon` | Run `docker context use default` |
| Port 80 bind error | Use `8080:80` in docker-compose.yml |
| `InvalidByte` on login | Check JWT key `\\n` replacement in `config.py` |
| `400 Bad Request` on login | Ensure admin email does not use `.local` TLD |
| `AssertionError` on startup | Remove `-> None` from all HTTP 204 route functions |

wiki.title: Known issues and fixes log
wiki.content:
# Known issues and fixes log

This page records every environment bug found during initial setup, the root cause, and the fix applied.

---

## FIX-001: Docker context pointing to Docker Desktop pipe

**Symptom:** `docker ps` fails with `Cannot connect to the Docker daemon`.

**Root cause:** A stale `desktop-linux` context pointed to `npipe:////./pipe/dockerDesktopLinuxEngine` (Docker Desktop, not installed).

**Fix:** `docker context use default` then `docker context rm desktop-linux`.

---

## FIX-002: email-validator rejects .local TLD

**Symptom:** Login returns HTTP 401 "Invalid credentials" even with correct password.

**Root cause:** `pydantic[email]` uses `email-validator` which rejects `.local` as a reserved/special-use TLD. Admin seed user never created.

**Fix:** Changed `ADMIN_EMAIL` from `admin@wztrack.local` to `admin@wztrack.io` in `.env` and `docker-compose.yml`. Reset volume with `docker compose down -v`.

---

## FIX-003: FastAPI assertion error on 204 routes

**Symptom:** API container fails to start with `AssertionError` from FastAPI internals.

**Root cause:** FastAPI 0.111+ asserts no response body on 204 routes. Functions annotated `-> None` are interpreted as having a `NoneType` response model.

**Fix:** Removed `-> None` from all six affected route functions: `auth.py`, `issues.py`, `projects.py`, `testcases.py`, `users.py`, `wiki.py`.

---

## FIX-004: bcrypt 4.x incompatible with passlib 1.7.4

**Symptom:** `AttributeError` or password verification failure at login.

**Root cause:** `bcrypt` 4.x rejects passwords longer than 72 bytes (passlib's wrap-bug detection uses a 73-byte test). passlib 1.7.4 was not updated to handle this.

**Fix:** Pinned `bcrypt==3.2.2` in `requirements.txt`.

---

## FIX-005: JWT PEM key double-escape in .env

**Symptom:** `InvalidByte` or `InvalidKeyError` when verifying JWT tokens after login.

**Root cause:** `.env` stores PEM newlines as `\n` (backslash + n). `pydantic-settings` reads this as a literal two-character sequence `\n`. The `config.py` property was replacing single `\n` which matched nothing.

**Fix:** Changed `jwt_private_key_pem` and `jwt_public_key_pem` properties to `replace("\\\\n", "\n")`.

---

## FIX-006: Rancher Desktop owns port 80 on Windows

**Symptom:** `docker compose up` fails with `bind: address already in use` on port 80.

**Root cause:** Rancher Desktop's `host-switch.exe` process binds port 80 on Windows host.

**Fix:** Changed frontend port mapping from `80:80` to `8080:80`. Updated `CORS_ORIGINS` to include `http://localhost:8080`.

---

## FIX-007: nginx strips port from Host header causing CORS redirect failure

**Symptom:** Browser console: `Access to XMLHttpRequest blocked by CORS policy` after redirect from `/api/v1/projects` to `http://localhost/api/v1/projects/`.

**Root cause:** FastAPI issues a trailing-slash redirect. nginx was forwarding `Host: localhost` (no port) via `$host`. FastAPI built the redirect URL using the portless host, sending the browser to port 80.

**Fix:** Changed `proxy_set_header Host $host` to `proxy_set_header Host $http_host` in `nginx.conf`. `$http_host` preserves the port from the original request.

wiki.title: Docker Compose service reference
wiki.content:
# Docker Compose service reference

## Services

### db (wztrack-db)

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Image | `postgres:16-alpine` |
| Port | not exposed to host |
| Volume | `wztrack_pgdata` |
| Health check | `pg_isready` — 5 s interval, 10 retries |

### api (wztrack-api)

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Image | built from `backend/Dockerfile` |
| Port | `8000:8000` |
| Depends on | `db` (healthy) |
| Runtime | Python 3.12-slim + uvicorn |
| Key config | `DATABASE_URL`, `JWT_PRIVATE_KEY`, `JWT_PUBLIC_KEY`, `ADMIN_EMAIL` |

### frontend (wztrack-fe)

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Image | built from `frontend/Dockerfile` (Node 20 build + nginx 1.27 runtime) |
| Port | `8080:80` |
| Proxy rule | `/api/` → `http://api:8000` |
| Key config | `proxy_set_header Host $http_host` in `nginx.conf` |

## Volumes

| Name | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `wztrack_pgdata` | PostgreSQL data directory |
| `wztrack_uploads` | Issue file attachments |

## Common commands

```bash
# Start all services
docker compose up -d

# Rebuild and restart a single service
docker compose up -d --build frontend

# Wipe database and reseed
docker compose down -v && docker compose up -d

# Tail API logs
docker compose logs -f api

# Open a psql shell
docker exec -it wztrack-db psql -U wztrack -d wztrack
```
